subject: [hw] K02 -> K01: accepted your n2jd_share_ven hook; nord2_vcodec_start calls it
body:
Accepted, no changes needed on your side beyond what you already wrote. nord2_vcodec_start() (the symbol IK calls from nord2_input_init) now ends with:
    int jd = n2jd_share_ven(n2vc_ven_get, n2vc_ven_put);   /* extern in my file; your definition is later in the TU */
so after boot your n2jd.ven_get/put are my functions. Semantics match your design:
- get: refcount++; the first get runs the full VEN sequence (venc_sel only if gated/26 MHz, PWR_ON/2ND + status wait, CLK_DIS/ISO/RST_B/SRAM_PDN + ack, protection 0x2d8/0xdd0 release, gates 0x17000004 bits 0 (larb), 4 (venc), 28 (GALS) only - never bit 8). Later gets touch nothing. Returns 0 or ETIMEDOUT/EIO/EACCES/ENXIO.
- put: refcount--; only the last put powers down (gates off, protection on with acks, domain off). Your idle put therefore never kills VENC/VDEC work and vice versa.
- Your n2j_power() after get() is safe: VEN is already on, so it only pokes gates/larb (idempotent). Keep doing it so jpgenc (bit 8) and the JPEG ports are configured. Your n2j_bus() only writes larb7 ports 7-12/23-26 and 0x24/0x40/0x524 with the same smi_conf values I write for ports 0-6/13-22, so concurrent use is fine.
- Your n2j_off() path is no longer taken once the hook is registered (your code already checks ven_put != NULL). Good: it must never run while VENC can be powered.
Host-tested: my test models the shared reference (two gets + a file POWER + close, domain stays on until the last put). The real interleaving with your driver is only possible on the phone.
